newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-Daimler chief lays ghosts of 1996 at AGM.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Daimler chief lays ghosts of 1996 at AGM.

text.p: Daimler-Benz AG Chairman Juergen Schrempp went before the company's shareholders on Wednesday promising "substantial" increases in profits and sales this year in remarks that helped erase memories of huge losses last year.

In a speech delivered at the company's annual general meeting, Schrempp proudly said, "the group is now active in businesses marked above all by healthy, self-sustaining growth and high profit potential."

Only a year ago, Schrempp went before angry shareholders to apologise for racking up the biggest loss in corporate German history and for not being able to pay a dividend for the first time in more than four decades.

Where last year Schrempp and the Daimler board faced the prospect of law suits for not disclosing the size of losses, Daimler management received congratulations from shareholders who encouraged them to stay what has at times been a difficult course.

The bright outlook comes amid growing confidence that a sweeping reorganisation earlier this year will result in a sharply more efficient management structure and as sales in the first four months of this year climbed 15 percent.

"Although this year will be dominated by numerous product launches along with the implementation of programs to optimise business operations, we assume that we can achieve a substantial improvement in operating profit," Schrempp said.
Daimler-Benz, Germany's largest company, reported an operating profit for 1996 of 2.423 billion marks ($1.4 billion), up from a loss of 7.197 billion marks in 1996.
Schrempp added that sales for the year as a whole should be "substantially" above last year's 106.34 billion marks.
In the first four months of 1997, Daimler said group sales jumped 15 percent to 36.3 billion marks as all the company's major divisions posted higher turnover.

Daimler-Benz's aerospace operations posted the fastest sales growth in the first four months of this year with turnover climbing 39 percent to 3.9 billion marks, largely on the back of its aircraft and space systems operations.
The backbone of Daimler-Benz, its Mercedes-Benz car and truck business, also showed double-digit sales growth between January and April this year.
Passenger car sales climbed 14 percent to 16.2 billion marks while commercial vehicle sales advanced 15 percent to 11.6 billion marks.

Schrempp said he expected to sell more than 700,000 cars this year, the highest ever, and that the company's share of the world car market is set to climb to 2.2 percent in the coming years from 1.6 percent now.
Schrempp also repeated his belief that Daimler will be able to achieve its goal of 12 percent return on capital employed within two years.
The sales growth comes as Daimler is making big strides toward redcing costs and making itself more efficient in the world market place.
As of April 1, Daimler's car and truck making unit Mercedes-Benz AG was merged into the corporate structure in an effort to speed up decision making and cut overhead.

Although Schrempp has been heavily criticised for such bold strokes, he won shareholders and analysts over with the move, promising on Wednesday that management will be 40 percent more efficient as a result of the management overhaul.
Schrempp said, however, that Daimler still had not achieved its financial goals and planned to step up its efforts, especially in Asia, but also in Latin America and Central and Eastern Europe.
"We must raise our profile and further sieze the opportunity for growth," Schrempp said.
($ = 1.702 German Marks)
